name: page-header
title: Page header
purpose: The top of a view: its title, an optional one-line description and the view's one optional primary action.
whenToUse: Once, at the top of a view's content, to say what the view is.
With the action when the view has one main thing to do, such as New task on the task list.
In the compact variant above a board, a transcript or a diff, where the content needs the height.
whenNotToUse: For the bar across the top of the app with the product name and the back link. Use an app header.
For the heading of a section inside a view. Use a plain h2.
For a second or third action. Put those in the view as secondary buttons, or behind a menu.
For help text of more than a line. Put it in the view or link to the documentation.

variants.name: default
variants.use: The title at 24px at every width, the size of a plain h1. Use it on most views.

variants.name: compact
variants.use: The title at 16px with a 12px description, for a dense screen. Pair it with a small button. A plain h2 is drawn larger than this title, so under a compact header head sections with h3 or with component titles, which are no larger than it.

accessibility: Use a header element, with the title as the view's one h1. The app header above it shows the product name, which is a link and not a heading. When the app header shows the view title in ds-app-header__title instead, that title is the h1 and the page header is left out. Never write both.
Head the sections under it with h2, which the base layer draws a step smaller than the title, or with the titles of the components they hold.
The description is a p directly after the title, one sentence long.
The action is one button, or one link styled as a button when it goes to another view. It may be the view's primary button, and then no other button in the view is primary.
In the compact variant use ds-button--small, which keeps a 44px pointer target.
On a narrow screen the action moves below the text instead of squeezing it. A long title wraps and is never cut.
The header adds no keyboard behaviour. Tab reaches the action in document order, after the title and description.
